chunks: Ibn Abi Umayr from al-Hasan ibn 'Atiyyah from 'Umar ibn Yazid, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about spending the dirhams that are carried upon them [i.e., silver dirhams], so he said: 'When the silver reaches the equivalent of the two [mithqals of gold], there is no harm [in spending it as gold currency].'

key_terms.الْمَحْمُولِ عَلَيْهَا: Carried upon them (referring to the silver content)
key_terms.الْمِثْلَيْنِ: The two equivalents (referring to the weight/value standard)

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for spending silver dirhams according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the criteria for the validity of silver dirhams in commercial transactions, establishing that their acceptability hinges on the equivalence of their intrinsic silver weight to two mithqals of gold. This ruling reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on *mithl* (comparable value) and *qimma* (market value) in currency exchange, ensuring fairness in trade by preventing riba (usury) through precise weight standards. It underscores the practical application of monetary law in early Islamic society, where the physical composition of coins determined their legal status as valid mediums of exchange.
